newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell moves to cut Nigerian gas flaring.
newsitem.headline: Shell moves to cut Nigerian gas flaring.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of oil giant Shell, attacked by environmentalists over its operations in Nigeria, said on Monday it had awarded a $320 million contract for the construction of a plant to reduce gas flaring.
The contract was awarded to the Japan Gasoline Company and Italy's Saipem consortium to build the plant at Shell's Soku oil field in the southeastern Rivers state, Shell said.

"The project is one of a series of initiatives planned by Shell on behalf of its joint venture partners (state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp) NNPC, Elf and Agip to end unnecessary gas flaring in the company's operations as soon as possible," it said in a statement.
Most Nigerian gas is currently flared in the process of producing crude oil. This means the gas is burnt off when the oil is extracted.

Shell, which pumps about half Nigeria's nearly two million barrels per day of crude oil, has been attacked over its operations here since last November when the authorities defied international opinion and hanged nine minority rights activists from the oil-producing Ogoniland for murder.
The activists, among them author Ken Saro-Wiwa, accused Shell of polluting the environment.
A $4 billion Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) plant is being built in Bonny, Rivers state to gather and export gas from 1999 and Shell is technical leader of the project.

Pressure groups like Greenpeace mounted a campaign to force Shell to withdraw from the LNG project, Africa's biggest construction project but the company refused saying the LNG would help curb gas flaring and reduce pollution.
Shell is contracted to supply gas processed at the new plant in Soku to the LNG plant.

"The problem of gas flaring is not something Shell can address on its own," Shell Nigeria managing director Brian Anderson said, adding Nigeria must provide fiscal incentives in order to utilise its gas reserves and end wasteful flaring.
The Soku plant is part of a complex of gas facilities that will gather gas from three Shell oil fields, nearly half from the company's flare lines.
Shell Nigeria said it aimed to develop two other projects to tap over a third of the gas it currently flares.
